scenes.heading: Execution Memory
scenes.narration: Let's take a deep look at Execution Memory and how it works under the hood in Spark.

scenes.heading: What execution memory powers
items: Join hash tables and sort buffers
Spills to disk when it overflows
scenes.narration: Execution memory is the working space Spark uses during computation, holding shuffle write buffers, aggregation hash maps, join hash tables, and sort buffers. It is the region under pressure whenever a task does heavy transformation work. When execution memory is exhausted, Spark spills intermediate data to disk rather than crashing.

scenes.heading: What happens under pressure
scenes.narration: When a task needs more execution memory, Spark first borrows any idle storage space and, if necessary, evicts cached blocks. If it still cannot fit the working set, it spills sorted or aggregated data to local disk and continues. Spilling keeps the job alive but adds disk I/O and serialization overhead, which shows up as slow, disk-bound tasks in the UI.

scenes.code:
# A wide aggregation that stresses execution memory
big = spark.read.parquet("/data/events")
agg = big.groupBy("key").agg({"amount": "sum"})
agg.write.parquet("/out/agg")
# In Spark UI, watch 'Spill (Memory)' and 'Spill (Disk)' per task
scenes.heading: Recognizing spill
scenes.narration: A wide aggregation like this builds large hash maps that consume execution memory. If a task's group data exceeds its share, you will see nonzero Spill Memory and Spill Disk metrics for that task in the Spark UI. Frequent spilling is a signal to increase parallelism, reduce data per partition, or give executors more memory. It is the clearest symptom of execution-memory pressure.

scenes.heading: Spill vs OOM
scenes.narration: Spilling is Spark's graceful safety valve: the job keeps running, just slower. An OutOfMemory error is a hard failure where a task or whole executor dies, usually from skew, oversized rows, or a broadcast that was too big. The remedy for spill is more or smaller partitions; the remedy for OOM is fixing the root cause, such as skew or an overlarge broadcast.

scenes.text: Persistent spill means partitions are too big; raise parallelism.
scenes.narration: Increasing shuffle partitions or repartitioning to smaller chunks usually cures chronic spilling without adding hardware.
